title: Cofactor‐Inspired Second‐Sphere Engineering of Artificial Metalloenzymes for Neutral Ammonia Synthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Constructing artificial metalloenzymes with precisely positioned metal centers and tailored second‐sphere microenvironments remains challenging in replicating the hierarchical catalytic functions of natural enzymes. Here, we report a cofactor‐inspired second‐sphere engineering strategy to construct an artificial nanozyme, CuS 1 /CN, featuring atomically defined [3Cu−1S] motifs selectively anchored to ultrasmall Cu clusters (∼0.73 nm) within a mesoporous nitrogen‐doped carbon framework. This architecture establishes enzyme‐like catalytic compartmentalization without compromising active‐site accessibility: exposed Cu sites mimic nitrate reductase for nitrate activation and water dissociation, while adjacent [3Cu−1S] motifs function as cofactor‐like centers that orchestrate interfacial hydration, facilitating proton‐coupled electron transfer and hydrogen relay during downstream hydrogenation. The engineered second‐sphere microenvironment overcomes the intrinsic *NO 2 ‐to‐*NO 2 H bottleneck and shifts the rate‐determining step to *NH 2 O‐to‐*NH 2 OH conversion with a substantially reduced energy barrier. Consequently, CuS 1 /CN enables highly efficient and selective ammonia electrosynthesis under neutral conditions at industrially relevant current densities with long‐term stability. Its integration into a Zn−NO 3 − battery further enables simultaneous nitrate conversion and electricity generation. This work establishes cofactor‐inspired second‐sphere engineering as a general strategy for designing artificial enzymes with programmable catalytic microenvironments beyond conventional active‐site engineering.

title: Electrochemically Directed Orientation in Two-Dimensional Conductive Metal-Organic Framework Thin Films
abstract: Controlling the preferred crystallographic orientation of two-dimensional (2D) conductive metal-organic framework (c-MOF) films is essential for maximizing anisotropic charge transport and unlocking their full potential in advanced applications. However, the factors governing film orientation during electrochemical growth on a substrate remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that the preferred orientation of amine-derived Ni3(HITP)2 films can be modulated by small changes in applied potential during anodic electrodeposition. Films deposited at 0.05 V exhibit smooth morphologies and pronounced (002) texture, consistent with preferential alignment of the layered framework parallel to the substrate. Increasing the potential to 0.10 V suppresses the dominant (002) contribution and increases the relative prominence of low-angle reflections associated with (100) family, indicating a shift in preferred orientation toward (100). Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy confirm that both films retain similar Ni-HITP framework chemistry and Ni coordination environments. Electrochemical measurements reveal distinct potential-dependent growth kinetics, with 0.05 V exhibiting slower, more gradual precursor activation and 0.10 V producing a larger, earlier current response consistent with more rapid generation of reactive species. Extension to catechol-derived Cu3(HHTP)2 reveals analogous potential-dependent changes in morphology, diffraction behavior, and electrochemical growth response. These findings establish applied potential as a practical parameter for modulating growth behavior and preferred crystallographic orientation in electrochemically deposited 2D c-MOF films.

title: Macrocycle 2D COF Single Crystal
abstract: Abstract We report the synthesis of a two-dimensional (2D) covalent organic framework (COF) single crystal, termed COF-900, constructed from a geminiarene-type macrocycle linker, biphenyl-extended pillar[3]arene containing nine phenyl units. The atomically accurate structure was resolved by three-dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED) of the 2D COF single crystal with a resolution of 1.2 Å, unveiling the conformation of the macrocycle in the layered backbone as well as AB interlayer stacking. The macrocycle exhibits a similar stacking mode in both the COF and the molecular crystal of the linker, suggesting prealignment of linkers during COF crystal growth through a mechanism termed alignment-led framework assembly (ALFA). Cryo-transmission electron microscopy images further provided direct real-space visualization of the macrocycle, where three types of interconnected pores were clearly visualized with sizes of 1.1, 1.5, and 2.3 nm.

title: Guest-Mediated On-Surface Growth of 2D COF Heterobilayer for Synaptic Devices
abstract: Abstract Chemically defined organic heterobilayers offer a route to programmable interfacial coupling, yet their on-surface construction remains challenging due to the instability of dynamic covalent frameworks during sequential growth. Here, we report a guest-induced COF-on-COF growth strategy that enables deterministic heteroepitaxy of imine/boroxine covalent organic framework (COF) heterobilayers at solid–liquid interfaces. Coronene guest molecules occupy the pores of the underlying imine COF, stabilizing the framework while promoting interfacial molecular diffusion, thereby redirecting growth from framework degradation to directional epitaxy. This yields a structurally precise heterobilayer with a commensurate √3 × √3 R30° rotational relationship and long-range order. The resulting 2D COF heterobilayer is continuous over large areas with low defect density, enabling direct device integration without transfer. Electrical measurements, supported by theory, reveal interfacial charge redistribution arising from chemically encoded asymmetry, manifested as interfacial charge redistribution and enhanced charge trapping. Device responses, including nonvolatile switching and analogue conductance modulation, provide a macroscopic readout of the molecularly defined heterointerface. These results establish a route to programmable organic heterostructures in which interfacial growth, coupling, and electronic functionality are codesigned through molecular assembly.

title: Mesoporous Defect-Assisted Ce-Doped Cu-SSZ-13 Enabling Low-Temperature NH3–SCR via Enhanced Oxygen Transfer
abstract: Abstract Coupling efficient redox cycling with molecular diffusion in confined microporous environments remains a central challenge in zeolite catalysis. In Cu-exchanged SSZ-13 catalysts for NH3-assisted NOx reduction, low-temperature activity is limited by sluggish Cu redox interconversion and mass-transport constraints, while incorporation of secondary cations often intensifies pore-diffusion penalties. Herein, we show that defect-mediated mesostructuring enables the stable incorporation of atomically dispersed Ce species within Cu-SSZ-13, forming a Cu–Ce adjacent structure that synergistically modulates transport and redox chemistry. In situ spectroscopic and isotope-labeling analyses combined with multiscale simulations reveal that the engineered defect network enhances NOx and NH3 diffusion, while Ce species anchored at defect-edge sites promote oxygen activation and accelerate Cu-NO2 intermediate formation. These effects collectively facilitate more efficient Cu2+/Cu+ cycling across a substantially broadened temperature window. The resulting catalyst achieves ≥90% NOx conversion between 147 and 560 °C. More broadly, this work establishes defect-enabled secondary-cation stabilization as a promising strategy to decouple diffusion limitations from redox optimization in confined catalytic systems.

title: Deferoxamine‐Engineered Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles Unlock High‐Valence Metal Channels for Multiplexed Mass Cytometry
abstract: ABSTRACT Mass cytometry (MC) enables highly multiplexed single‐cell protein analysis, but its full analytical potential remains constrained by the limited range of available mass tags. Here, we report deferoxamine‐engineered mesoporous silica nanoparticles (DFO‐MSNs) for high‐capacity loading of multiple underutilized high‐valent metal ions within a common nanoparticle scaffold. DFO‐MSNs accommodated Zr 4+ , Hf 4+ , Nb 5+ , and Ta 5+ at approximately 10 4 metal atoms per nanoparticle, with high metal retention in physiological buffers. Following PEGylation and antibody (Ab) conjugation, the resulting Zr‐, Nb‐, Hf‐, and Ta‐based probes enabled antigen‐specific detection of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) by co‐staining with commercial Maxpar reagents. Nb‐, Hf‐, and Ta‐loaded MSN_CD8a probes resolved CD8a+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes at titers as low as 30 NPs/cell. In a 30‐plex staining panel, Ta@MSN_CD25 resolved low‐abundance CD25 hi CD127 lo T reg ‐like cells with apparent population recovery comparable to the corresponding Maxpar reagent, while consuming ca. 35‐fold less Ab. Together, these results establish a modular strategy for incorporating underutilized high‐valent metals into functional mass tags and demonstrate the feasibility of integrating MSN‐based probes into multiplexed MC immunophenotyping workflows.

title: Zeolite Crystallization via Seed-Mediated Chemical Vapor Deposition
abstract: Abstract The demand for zeolites with specific, tailored characteristics is expected to further accelerate. For decades, however, zeolites have been predominantly synthesized by hydrothermal methods, in which tightly coupled sol–gel processes, nucleation, and crystal growth constrain property control and complicate device-oriented fabrication. Here we report the direct synthesis of zeolites by chemical vapor deposition (CVD), in which vapor-delivered precursors crystallize on preexisting zeolite seeds. Mechanistic investigations reveal that zeolite growth under CVD follows a fundamentally distinct pathway, where vapor-phase hydrolysis–condensation reactions are spatially decoupled from interfacial crystallization. This decoupling enables the maintenance of a controlled and steady supersaturation, offering a facile strategy for fabricating zeolite films with low dielectric constants and robust mechanical properties. The unique mechanism and operation mode of CVD bring zeolite crystallization into a manufacturing-relevant vapor-phase regime that could be extended to other zeolite types and deployed in diverse applications.

title: When Electrolytes Become Dopants: Programming Charge Transport in Conductive Metal−Organic Framework Transistors
abstract: Abstract Conjugated metal−organic frameworks (c-MOFs) operating in ionic environments have emerged as promising microporous and conductive systems for next-generation applications. Understanding the interplay between electrolyte composition and electronic−ionic mixed transport remains a critical barrier to the rational design of novel devices. Here, we demonstrate that electrolyte composition provides a direct and programmable handle for controlling charge transport and field-effect properties in c-MOF electrochemical transistors (ECTs). Two types of c-MOF thin films composed of the conjugated linker 2,3,5,6,10,11-hexahydroxytriphenylene (HHTP) and either Cu2+ or Ni2+ ions, namely, Cu3(HHTP)2 and Ni3(HHTP)2, were employed as transistor channel materials. Using these c-MOFs as prototypical conductive frameworks, we systematically interrogate the influence of ionic strength, ion identity, pH, and gate configuration on transistor operation. Across these variables, we unveil robust and quantitative relationships linking the nature and conditions of the electrolyte to variations in charge neutrality, modulation of transconductance, and transitions between transport regimes. For instance, increasing ionic strength shifts the transfer curves of Cu3(HHTP)2- and Ni3(HHTP)2-based ECTs toward a more negative potential, with a linear dependence on the logarithm of ion concentration. The ion-hydrated radius strongly influences ion-electron transport, as smaller cations more readily permeate the framework and reduce surface potential. Charge neutrality point potential (VCNP) displays a linear pH dependence, with sensitivities comparable to conducting polymer ECTs. Device performance is also influenced by the gate electrode configuration (liquid-junction or pseudo-reference electrodes). Extensive field-effect characterization demonstrates good electrochemical stability. A unified mechanistic model successfully describes the coupled ionic−electronic transport governing c-MOF device operation.

title: Atomic-Scale Mechanisms of Sequential Phase Transformation in Hydrogen-Driven Iron Oxide Reduction
abstract: Abstract Hydrogen-based direct reduction of iron oxides provides a carbon-free pathway to sustainable steelmaking, yet the atomistic mechanisms governing sequential reduction remain unresolved. Using in situ environmental transmission electron microscopy and density functional theory, we visualize the H2-driven reduction cascade from α-Fe2O3 through Fe3O4 to FeO at atomic resolution. The α-Fe2O3 → Fe3O4 transformation initiates at the surface and proceeds through inward migration of the α-Fe2O3/Fe3O4 interface, with no detectable Fe3O4 nucleation in the examined α-Fe2O3 interiors. The subsequent Fe3O4 → FeO transformation exhibits boundary-dependent behavior: FeO nucleates at defect-rich regions of the examined high-angle grain boundaries, whereas nanovoids form within the surrounding Fe3O4 bulk in association with low-angle boundaries. This contrast suggests that local defect structures influence local oxygen-vacancy accumulation and the competition between boundary FeO nucleation and bulk void formation. Atomistic calculations further show that interstitial hydrogen lowers oxygen-vacancy formation and migration barriers and promotes vacancy association. These results reveal how local crystallographic defects and interstitial hydrogen influence sequential iron oxide reduction through their effects on oxygen-vacancy formation, migration, and association.

title: De Novo Design of Single–Crystalline Peptide Frameworks Enables Structure–Encoded Molecular Recognition
abstract: Abstract Molecular recognition by proteins underlies many biological processes and depends on the precise spatial organization of functional residues within well-defined binding pockets. Synthetic peptide assembly, however, is frequently biased toward anisotropic fibrillar or other low-dimensional morphologies, owing in part to the directional nature of peptide hydrogen-bonding networks, which can hinder the formation of ordered, structurally encoded binding cavities with biomimetic recognition properties. Here we show that coordination-driven β-sheet reprogramming overcomes this constraint by redirecting peptide assembly into single-crystalline peptide frameworks. Through de novo peptide design, we incorporate tyrosine, a residue that often plays a key role in protein molecular recognition, as a functional side chain, while metal–peptide connectivity suppresses fibrillar growth and decouples backbone packing from side-chain organization, thereby orienting tyrosine residues along internal channel surfaces to generate chiral recognition environments. The resulting frameworks exhibit high chemical and mechanical robustness, allow the spatial organization of tyrosine residues to be resolved crystallographically, and display excellent stereoselective recognition performance toward structurally complex glucocorticoids and chiral pharmaceuticals. Molecular dynamics simulations suggest that tyrosine residues dynamically interact with guest molecules during recognition. Our findings provide a design principle for constructing crystalline peptide frameworks with biomimetic molecular recognition, expanding the structural and functional scope of synthetic peptide materials.

title: High-Throughput Screening of Photocatalytic Metal–Organic Frameworks for CO2 Reduction Using Relational Data Extraction and Hierarchical Machine Learning
abstract: Abstract Photocatalytic carbon dioxide reduction (CO2RR) over metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) is governed by both framework features and reaction conditions, which complicate catalyst discovery and render general design rules difficult to establish. In this study, we develop a synergistic machine-learning workflow to integrate literature data extraction, electronic-property prediction, and hierarchical classification for prioritizing MOF photocatalysts. First, a literature-derived record-level data set containing catalyst compositions, structural descriptors, reaction conditions, and catalytic outcomes was curated through large language model (LLM)-assisted relation extraction followed by manual verification. Then, a transfer-learning crystal graph convolutional neural network (CGCNN) model was trained for band gap prediction at the Heyd-Scuseria-Ernzerhof screened hybrid functional (HSE06) level, achieving a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.31 eV against reference HSE06 calculations. Subsequently, a physically constrained multitask framework was employed to predict electron affinity (EA) and ionization potential (IP) for thermodynamic prescreening. Three record-level classifiers were constructed for activity screening (C1), performance classification (C2), and product selectivity prediction (C3). When applied to the Computation-Ready, Experimental (CoRE) MOF database under standardized gas- and liquid-phase inference settings, the workflow prioritized 639 primary candidates, with most assigned to CO formation. Probability calibration and applicability-domain analysis further identified 166 of these candidates (25.98%) as a more stringent calibrated, in-domain subset. Overall, this study provides a practical data-driven workflow for condition-resolved prioritization of MOF photocatalysts and analysis of descriptor-level trends associated with photocatalytic CO2RR.

title: From Empirical Tuning to Predictive Design: Decoupling Dynamic Bottlenecks in Photocatalytic H 2 O 2 Production via Z‐Score Importance Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Deconvoluting the intertwined dynamic bottlenecks of photogenerated charge and reaction substrates remains a fundamental bottleneck in heterogeneous photocatalysis due to the lack of reasonable and effective tools. This study presents a quantitative, interpretable framework to deconvolve the entangled factors limiting solar‐driven photocatalysis. Using Au(I)‐based covalent metal‐organic framework (CMOF‐Au) isomers with controlled stacking (AA, AB, and ABC) as a model platform for hydrogen peroxide photosynthesis, we applied a Z‑score and LOFO (Leave‐One‐Feature‐Out) importance analysis. This approach revealed that the dominant rate‐determining factor shifts with stacking: bulk charge transfer governs performance in AA stacking, whereas surface adsorption limits AB and ABC stacking. The method successfully quantifies the relative contribution weights of key functions (charge dynamics, interfacial transfer, surface adsorption, and mass transport) and demonstrates high predictive power across diverse photocatalysts, including covalent organic frameworks, porous aromatic frameworks, C 3 N 4 , and overall water‐splitting systems. By uncovering counterintuitive mechanisms, such as Simpson's paradox, our work establishes a generalizable strategy for decoupling multivariate factors, moving photocatalyst design from empirical tuning toward a predictive, function‐aware paradigm.

title: Electronic Polarization of Covalent Organic Framework Membranes for Precise Antibiotic Purification
abstract: Abstract Precise molecular separation is essential for pharmaceutical production and purification, yet existing sieving systems struggle to distinguish structurally similar molecules due to their predominant reliance on size exclusion. Herein, we fabricate a covalent organic framework (COF) membrane featuring fluorine-induced polarized nanochannels for fast organic solvent nanofiltration. The incorporation of fluorine atoms redistributes electron density along the pore walls, creating a polarized electrostatic environment while lowering surface energy. This unique pore environment promotes the uptake and transport of polar solvents, while enhancing separation selectivity by retarding highly polar solutes through polarity-dependent solute-framework interactions. Furthermore, the low surface energy imparted by the robust C–F bonds also reduces irreversible foulant adhesion and facilitates permeance recovery after cleaning. The resultant COF membrane achieves a molecular weight cutoff down to 350 Da and stable operation for over 550 h. Notably, it differentiates structurally related fluoroquinolone antibiotics according to their molecular polarity and delivers a favorable separation factor of 8.9 for norfloxacin over its synthetic intermediate piperazine. This work demonstrates that engineering pore-wall polarity in COF membranes provides a viable route to chemically regulated molecular recognition beyond size-based separation.

title: Engineering Amino‐Induced p‐π Conjugation for Electronic Regulation of Li + Transport in PVDF‐Based Solid‐State Electrolytes
abstract: ABSTRACT Sluggish Li + transport in poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF)‐based solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) arises from restricted polymer segmental motion and persistent Li + ‐FSI − association, while conventional fillers provide limited regulation of the local electronic and coordination environments. Herein, amino‐functionalized UiO66‐NH 2 is introduced into a PVDF/lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (LiFSI) electrolyte to construct electronically active composite SPEs (U6NP). The electron‐donating ─NH 2 groups induce p‐π conjugation, redistribute the linker electron density, and strengthen ligand‐to‐metal charge transfer (LMCT)‐related electronic coupling between the organic linkers and Zr‐O clusters. This electronic reconstruction, together with amino‐associated modulation of local O‐centered coordination environments, reshapes the electrostatic landscape, weakens Li + ‐FSI − interactions, and facilitates Li + migration. U6NP delivers a room‐temperature ionic conductivity of 2.41 × 10 −3 S cm −1 , a Li + transference number of 0.56, and an oxidative stability of 4.42 V. More importantly, Li||U6NP||LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 (NCM811) cells with a cathode loading of 21.5 mg cm −2 retain 98.51% after 120 cycles at 0.05 C. The Li||U6NP||NCM811 pouch cell delivers 136.6 mAh g −1 initially and 120.9 mAh g −1 after 100 cycles. This work establishes ─NH 2 ‐induced p‐π conjugation‐enhanced LMCT as an effective strategy for electronically active MOF‐reinforced PVDF electrolytes toward high‐loading solid‐state lithium metal batteries.

title: Mitochondria‐Inspired COF Nanochannels for Reversible Directional Ion Transport for Osmotic Power Generation
abstract: ABSTRACT Directional ion transport in artificial nanochannels usually relies on fixed structural or chemical asymmetry, which restricts adaptive regulation. Inspired by proton transport in mitochondrial ATP synthase, we fabricate pH‐responsive PAN‐supported COF nanochannel membranes via liquid–liquid confined interfacial polymerization. Transmembrane pH polarization triggers asymmetric charge regulation and builds an internal electric field. The membranes show pH‐dependent ion transport, with conductance spanning 0.4–1005.5 µS and a forward/reverse power density ratio of 202. Under a 100‐fold NaCl gradient and pH 1/13 polarization, they deliver 20.2 W m − 2 . Experiments verify pH‐dependent COF charge regulation, while simulations indicate internal electric fields modulate ion migration together with diffusion. Salinity and pH gradients supply transport driving force; COF charge regulation dominates directional transport, and electrolyte properties, ion mobilities and electrochemical potentials tune current and output power. The observation of analogous directional transport across six chemically distinct membrane systems suggests the broader applicability of pH‐mediated transport regulation. These results provide insight into adaptive ion regulation and a strategy for energy conversion under combined salinity and pH gradients.

title: Engineering Stable and Targeted NIR/SWIR Imaging Agents through Metal-Organic Framework Nanoconfinement
abstract: Near-infrared (NIR) and shortwave infrared (SWIR) fluorophores offer significant potential for biomedical imaging owing to their deep tissue penetration and low background autofluorescence. However, their widespread application remains limited by poor aqueous solubility, aggregation-induced fluorescence loss, and inadequate stability in physiological environments. Here, we present a general nanoconfinement strategy that converts hydrophobic molecular fluorophores into stable, bright, and engineerable imaging nanocomposites through encapsulation within the large-pore metal-organic framework ZIF-71. Using IR-780 as a model dye and extending the approach to the larger fluorophores IR-813 and IR-1048, we demonstrate that in situ encapsulation preserves a predominantly monomeric dye population within the ZIF-71 framework, effectively suppressing aggregation across diverse aqueous environments, including physiologically relevant and high-salinity conditions. Compared with free dyes and benchmark micellar formulations, the IR-780@ZIF composites exhibit markedly improved resistance to aggregation, enhanced solution and photostability, and substantially increased fluorescence quantum yields and imaging brightness in water and phosphate-buffered saline. The benefits of confinement become increasingly pronounced for larger and more hydrophobic fluorophores, turning essentially dark free dyes IR-813 and IR-1048 in aqueous media into bright composites. Importantly, the external surface of the ZIF particles can be modified orthogonally through post-synthetic functionalization without compromising the optical properties of the encapsulated fluorophore. Surface incorporation of biotin and cell-penetrating peptide ligands enables tailored cellular delivery of the fluorophores, demonstrating the modularity of the platform. Collectively, these results establish large-pore ZIFs as versatile hosts for molecular NIR/SWIR fluorophores and highlight MOF nanoconfinement as a powerful strategy for integrating high-performance photophysics with customizable biological functionality for advanced imaging applications.

title: Self‐Assembly and Bimodal Chemical Activation of Dibromodibenzothiophene S ‐Oxide on Au(111)
abstract: ABSTRACT The rapidly growing on‐surface synthesis toolbox is currently developing toward reaction schemes of increasing complexity, namely by the use of polyfunctional and non‐planar precursors. We present an extensive experimental and theoretical investigation of the on‐surface self‐assembly and reactivity of dibromodibenzothiophene S ‐oxide on the Au(111) surface in ultrahigh vacuum in submonolayer regime. Several phases are observed after room‐temperature deposition depending on the coverage, with the dibenzothiophene backbone parallel to the surface and the oxygen pointing downward. Upon thermal activation, deoxygenation of the sulfoxide group and dissymmetric dehalogenation are sequentially initiated, leading to an unexpected organometallic intermediate phase with singly debrominated molecules. The deoxygenation reaction induces electronic structure modifications and chemical shifts in the sulfur as well as the carbon core levels. The final product after complete Ullmann coupling consists in dibenzothiophene nanoribbons. The importance of halogen bonding in the formation of “closed‐shell” clusters and in the stabilization of the singly debrominated domains is highlighted. Our results, based on scanning probe microscopy, x‐ray spectroscopy, and diffraction measurements, supported by theoretical modeling at the density functional theory level, provide insights into the intrinsic dependence of structure and reactivity in on‐surface synthesis.

title: Self-Assembly of Sub-10 nm Lamellar Domains with Controlled Orientation Using Fluorinated Junctions
abstract: Abstract We studied the thin-film self-assembly behavior of low-molecular-weight symmetric block copolymers (BCPs) of poly(solketal methacrylate) (PSM) and polystyrene (PS), with and without a poly(hexafluoroisopropyl acrylate) low-surface-energy (LSE) junction, PSM-b-F-b-PS and PSM-b-PS, respectively. An in situ hydrolysis of the PSM block to hydrophilic poly(glyceryl monomethacrylate) (PGM) markedly increased the segmental interaction parameter, χ. The high-χ, low-N copolymers self-assembled into horizontal or vertical lamellae with a center-to-center distance between adjacent lamellae (full pitch) of 9.4 nm. A free-energy analysis of the thin-film self-assembly on native Si predicted that the LSE junctions would induce an orientation of the lamellae for PGM-b-F-b-PS normal to the surface with only a few segments of the LSE junction. In comparison, an orientation of the lamellae parallel to the surface with an island-hole surface topography resulted from PGM-b-PS. We note that vertical lamellae were observed at the edges of islands and holes where the thickness transits from one thickness commensurate with the full pitch to another. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) and grazing-incidence small-angle X-ray scattering (GI-SAXS) results matched the free-energy predictions. With LSE junctions, uniform vertical orientation of the self-assembled lamellae was obtained, eliminating the need to modify the substrate or apply external fields to obtain this orientation, significantly simplifying preparation.

title: Fully integrated perovskite active polaritonic circuits
abstract: Abstract Photonic integrated circuits are emerging as a key technology for compact, analogue and energy-efficient optical information processing 1 . Yet, their practical implementation remains limited by the intrinsically weak optical nonlinearities of conventional materials, which demand high power and large device footprints to achieve substantial nonlinear responses 2 . Exciton–polaritons, hybrid light–matter excitations of semiconducting materials, offer a promising route to overcome these limitations by combining strong optical nonlinearities with the high speed and scalability typical of photonic platforms 3–5 . However, despite their potential, fully integrated on-chip polaritonic systems simultaneously delivering room-temperature waveguide lasing, controllable optical routing and amplification have remained elusive. Here we demonstrate a fully integrated perovskite polaritonic circuit that brings these functionalities together in a single-step-grown platform. We realize precise and scalable polariton circuits with integrated gratings that act as both couplers and reflectors, enabling in-plane Fabry–Pérot cavities. These structures support robust in-plane polariton lasing with coherent guided emission at a geometry-defined wavelength, optical amplification of propagating polaritons and nonlinear optical phase control exceeding π, all within the same on-chip architecture. Our results establish perovskite polariton circuits as a scalable platform for active and interferometric integrated photonics.

title: Antiaromaticity for Through-Space Molecular Thermoelectricity
abstract: Abstract Charge transport in molecular junctions has largely relied on aromatic frameworks, where intramolecular π-delocalization stabilizes the electronic structure but inherently limits intermolecular electronic coupling. Here we show that antiaromatic Ni(II) norcorrole assemblies outperform their aromatic counterparts in thermally driven charge transport. This superior performance arises from strong intermolecular coupling, facilitated by the externalized electronic stabilization of antiaromatic building blocks. Such strong intermolecular coupling enables unusually thick molecular stacks within molecular junctions and yields Seebeck coefficients of up to 600 μV K–1, far exceeding those of the aromatic analogue. Quantum transport calculations reveal that π–π stacking in the antiaromatic assemblies shifts the HOMO transmission resonance closer to the Fermi level while progressively narrowing it, accounting for the substantial enhancement of the Seebeck coefficient while maintaining efficient long-range charge transport with a low tunneling attenuation coefficient. These findings establish antiaromaticity as a design principle for thermoelectric energy conversion based on collective intermolecular coupling rather than isolated molecular orbitals.

title: Inorganic Ionic Polymerization toward Fracture-Resistant, Self-healable Functional Hydrogels
abstract: Abstract Fracture-resistant, self-healable functional hydrogels hold promise for soft robotics, wearable electronics, and intelligent devices. However, integrating these properties within a single structure remains challenging. Persistent load-bearing constraints hinder molecular rearrangement for repair, whereas excessive network dynamics can disrupt functional organization. Here, we uncover a reciprocal assembly mechanism based on bidirectional regulation between inorganic ionic oligomers and polymer chains. The acrylic acid/poly(acrylic acid) (PAA) environment suppresses calcium carbonate oligomer (CCO) aggregation, while CCO organizes PAA chains into birefringent acicular domains through multisite coordination and cooperative hydrogen bonding. These domains provide persistent load-bearing constraints and exchangeable interactions, enabling a fracture energy of 38.3 kJ m–2 and 87% tensile-strength recovery after 6 h of ambient healing. The same assembled network further exhibits 4.5% AM1.5G solar-weighted absorptivity and strong mid-infrared emission, remaining 5.1 °C cooler than neat PAA under simulated sunlight while retaining its cooling response for 21 days. This work establishes inorganic ionic oligomers as active reciprocal regulators of polymer organization, coupling dynamic network reconstruction with mechanical reinforcement and functional stability.

title: A Metal–Organic Framework-on-Metal–Organic Framework Chemical Nose for Intelligent Identification of Depression-Related Biomarkers via Machine Learning
abstract: Abstract Depression is a complex mental disorder associated with dysregulation of multiple neurotransmitter-related biomarkers, including Try, 5-HT, 5-HIAA, and 5-HTP. Herein, we report a MOF-on-MOF fluorescent sensor array, RhB@ZIF-8-on-FL@UiO-67, for simultaneous discrimination and detection of these biomarkers. Spatial separation of dyes within the hierarchical architecture effectively suppresses fluorescence crosstalk and generates multiple independent luminescent channels, enhancing signal diversity and sensing performance. The resulting multidimensional fluorescence responses enable accurate identification of Try, 5-HT, 5-HIAA, 5-HTP, and their mixtures. Both LDA and HCA achieved a classification accuracy of 100% for the tested samples. Furthermore, machine learning models, including BP, RF, DT, SVM, and KNN, confirmed the robustness of the sensing platform. This work integrates MOF-on-MOF engineering with machine learning-assisted pattern recognition, offering a sensitive and reliable strategy for multiplex biomarker analysis and providing a promising approach for intelligent diagnosis of complex diseases.

title: Nanoscale Reduced‐Porphyrinic Covalent Organic Frameworks with Modulated Absorption for Enhanced Photodynamic Therapy
abstract: ABSTRACT Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) offer an attractive platform for organizing nanophotosensitizers into ordered architectures for improving photodynamic therapy (PDT). However, the photochemical performance of conventional porphyrin‐based frameworks has largely been constrained by their limited optical absorption at longer wavelength and inefficient generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS). Herein, we report the first highly crystalline nanoscale COFs (nCOFs) incorporating reduced porphyrin units, chlorins, and bacteriochlorins, which exhibit markedly modulated light absorption photophysical activity and PDT efficacy. Chlorin‐ and bacteriochlorin‐based nCOFs (Ctp and Btp) were prepared via imine condensation of high‐purity monomers under oxygen‐ and light‐free conditions at room temperature, affording long‐range crystalline order while preserving the intrinsic optical properties of the reduced chromophores. Compared to porphyrin‐based COF, Btp exhibited pronounced bathochromic shifts with strong absorption in the 640–750 nm region and substantially enhanced ROS generation under 705 and 808 nm laser irradiation. In Ctp‐ and Btp‐mediated PDT, the photocytotoxicity toward MC38 cancer cells was significantly enhanced, with potent antitumor efficacy in a murine colorectal tumor model. This study establishes reduced porphyrin as a viable building block for highly crystalline COFs and highlights the potential of ordered chromophore engineering for expanding the photochemical functionality of nCOFs.

title: Mechanocatalytic Upcycling of Diverse Plastic Wastes via an Fe/SiO 2 Catalyst
abstract: ABSTRACT Upcycling plastic waste into high‐value chemicals is an attractive pathway for the sustainable development of human society. Here, we demonstrate the mechanocatalytic conversion of polyethylene, polypropylene, polystyrene, polyester, and their mixtures into valuable hydrogen (H 2 ) and methane (CH 4 ) gases on an iron (Fe) species‐dispersed silica (SiO 2 ) catalyst, achieving almost 100% conversion under mild conditions. During the mechanocatalytic process, Fe species from the milling balls were anchored to the surface of pristine SiO 2 nanoparticles, forming the Fe/SiO 2 catalyst. Simultaneously, the Fe and Si sites in the Fe/SiO 2 catalyst synergistically facilitate the C─H bond activation and C─C bond cleavage pathways, enabling a favorable dehydrogenation‒cracking‒hydrogenation process to produce commercially valuable H 2 and CH 4 . Notably, this catalytic system also exhibits exceptional versatility in processing mixed plastic wastes without requiring prior sorting, while maintaining robust cycling stability. No expensive components, toxic chemicals, or energy‐intensive thermal conditions are needed.

title: Green Electrochemical Synthesis of Antimicrobial Polyaldehyde Starch
abstract: Abstract Conventional aldehyde-based biocides raise environmental and safety concerns due to their toxicity and persistence in inhibiting microbiologically influenced corrosion (MIC) in numerous industrial applications. The present study introduces a rapid and sustainable method for synthesizing polyaldehyde starch through electrochemistry (PAS-EC) using soluble starch as feedstock in aqueous salt media with iridium–ruthenium electrodes. This approach has the potential to replace toxic oxidants with a safer alternative, while significantly reducing reaction time and enhancing overall process safety. By minimizing hazardous reagents and streamlining operational steps, it can also contribute to improved sustainability. Taken together, these features make electrochemical methods a promising pathway for application in industrial bioprocesses. Under optimized electrochemical conditions (15 mA cm–2, 15% NaCl, and 1 h), PAS-EC was obtained with 65% yield and a degree of oxidation exceeding 63%, surpassing the conventional periodate-oxidized dialdehyde starch (DAS-PO) with 50% yield and a 48% degree of oxidation. FTIR and NMR characterization confirmed the successful formation of aldehydic groups, while thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) revealed a decrease in thermal stability due to the modification in the structure of pure starch. Biocidal efficacy was assessed against six hydrocarbon-degrading bacterial strains that are extremely relevant to MIC and bioremediation under oil and gas field conditions. PAS-EC displayed promising and broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, with a maximum of 60% inhibition efficiency at 1000 ppm in comparison to glutaraldehyde. Overall, both PAS-EC and DAS-PO demonstrated promising biocidal performance, underscoring their potential as safer and more sustainable alternatives.

title: Multiscale Modelling of Energy Materials
abstract: The conflicts between accuracy and efficiency of simulation have significantly limited the precision and scope of modelling in materials science. By integrating different computational techniques across various scales, it is possible to achieve a balance that enhances both precision and scope. This PhD thesis focuses on the multiscale modeling of energy materials, demonstrating the power and effectiveness of multiscale simulation in understanding and predicting material properties. The study covers a broad spectrum of materials and methodologies as given in graphical abstract, including density functional theory calculation (DFT) of organic-inorganic hybrid perovskites, molecular dynamics simulation of carbon-supported metal Ru nanoparticles, and the Monte-Carlo simulation of self-assembly of flurbiprofen molecules on metal surfaces. At the quantum scale, DFT calculations are employed to investigate the stability and electronic structure of halogen molecules intercalation in layered hybrid perovskites. For example, the manipulation of the bandgap and charge carrier mobility of layered perovskites through intercalation is explored, highlighting the impact of halogen bonding on the properties of such family of materials. At the atomic scale, Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations provide a detailed understanding of the morphology and stability of carbon-supported Ru nanoparticles. The simulations reveal how metal support interactions and metal structural arrangements influence the stability of these nanoparticles. At the mesoscale, Monte Carlo (MC) simulations capture the self-assembly behavior of flurbiprofen on metal surfaces. The simulations show how molecule-molecule interactions drive the formation of ordered nanostructures, offering insights into the design of materials with specific chiral properties. Overall, this thesis highlights the critical role of multiscale modeling in advancing the field of energy materials, offering a detailed understanding of material behavior across different scales.

title: An Integrated Coarse-Grained Simulation and Graph-Transformer Framework for the Discovery of Self-Assembling Cyclic Peptides
abstract: Abstract Self-assembling cyclic peptides are promising building blocks for functional biomaterials owing to their enhanced structural stability, proteolytic resistance, and diverse supramolecular architectures. However, how cyclization regulates peptide self-assembly remains poorly understood, and computational frameworks specifically developed for cyclic peptides are still lacking. Here, we demonstrate that disulfide-mediated cyclization fundamentally reshapes peptide self-assembly by significantly enhancing aggregation propensity (AP) and promoting the formation of diverse nanostructures compared with their linear counterparts, as confirmed by coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) simulations and experimental characterization. Motivated by these findings, we established an integrated computational-experimental framework for the prediction and rational design of self-assembling disulfide-cyclized peptides. A data set comprising 8,000 cyclic pentapeptides was generated using CGMD simulations, and multiple machine learning and deep learning models were systematically evaluated, among which a Graph-Transformer achieved the best predictive performance (R2 = 0.971). The optimized model was subsequently applied to high-throughput screening of 160,000 cyclic hexapeptides using a ranking strategy integrating AP and hydrophobicity, leading to the identification of multiple previously unreported self-assembling candidates. Experimental validation showed excellent agreement with model predictions. Furthermore, systematic sequence analysis revealed residue- and position-dependent assembly rules unique to disulfide-cyclized peptide systems. This work establishes a computational framework for the rapid discovery of self-assembling disulfide-cyclized peptides and provides new mechanistic insights and design principles for peptide-based functional materials.

title: End-Group Functionalization Reshapes the Self-Assembly and Phase Behavior of Pluronic F68 in Water
abstract: Abstract Pluronic triblock copolymers based on poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) and poly(propylene oxide) (PPO), with a PEO–PPO–PEO architecture, exhibit thermoresponsive self-assembly governed by the interplay among polymer hydration, micellization, and intermicellar organization. Here, we investigate how terminal bisurethane-methacrylate functionalization affects the aqueous self-assembly and phase behavior of Pluronic F68. The resulting derivative, termed F68-XL, was examined over broad concentration and temperature ranges using differential scanning calorimetry, rheology, small-angle X-ray scattering, and refractive-index measurements. End-group functionalization produces only modest changes in the micellization boundary but markedly alters the conditions under which higher-order micellar organization develops. Compared with pristine F68, F68-XL displays a displacement of the body-centered cubic ordered region toward higher temperatures and polymer concentrations, together with an unusual re-entrant liquid-like–solid-like–liquid-like rheological response at high concentrations. These findings indicate that terminal functionalization affects higher-order organization more strongly than primary micellization and highlight the sensitivity of intermicellar packing and phase stability to Pluronic chain-end chemistry. The photoreactive terminal groups additionally enable UV-induced covalent network formation, establishing the photo-cross-linking capability of F68-XL. Overall, this work identifies end-group functionalization as an effective strategy for modulating the thermoresponsive self-assembly and phase behavior of Pluronic F68 while introducing an additional route to covalent network formation.

title: Aromatic Substituent Engineering of Polypeptides for Tunable Self-Assembly and Multicolor Solution- and Aggregation-State Emissions
abstract: Abstract Luminescent polypeptides and corresponding nanoparticles with tunable morphology and luminescent colors have shown significant potential in optical encoding and bioimaging. Herein, a series of aromatic substituent-modified poly(l-glutamate) bearing dihydrodibenzothiophene, carbazole, and triphenylamine moieties are synthesized. Despite the same peptide backbone, these polypeptides exhibit green, yellow, and orange luminescence centered at 509, 604, and 681 nm in solution, respectively. Time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy reveals emission lifetimes of 113.7, 121.2, and 108.9 μs of the polypeptides, while the fluorescence quantum yields (Qy) are 4.0%, 9.3%, and 3.1%, respectively. Upon self-assembly, nanobowls and large compound micelles with emission wavelengths located at 501, 554, and 629 nm are obtained, which are significantly blue-shifted compared with that of the polypeptides. Benefiting from their tunable multicolor emission, these polypeptides are further demonstrated for luminescent anti-counterfeiting. This study provides a facile side-chain substitution strategy for constructing luminescent polypeptides with controlled emission in both solution and aggregation states.

title: Hierarchical Charge Confinement in Metallo‐Supramolecular Rings Enables Bistable Electrochromism With Long Optical Memory
abstract: ABSTRACT Bistable electrochromic devices retain a programmed optical state after removal of the driving bias, but their bleached states often decay through charge back‐transfer, compensating‐ion migration, and self‐discharge. Here, ligand‐angle programming and side‐group engineering are combined to construct linear metallo‐supramolecular assemblies (LMSA), cyclic metallo‐supramolecular assemblies (CMSA), and tert‐butyl‐substituted cyclic metallo‐supramolecular assemblies (t‐CMSA) from a common Fe‐terpyridine chromophore. Ring formation interrupts long‐range charge‐transport pathways, whereas tert‐butyl groups weaken inter‐ring π–π contacts and electronic coupling and create an open packing environment that stabilizes compensating anions. This topology‐to‐packing evolution establishes hierarchical charge confinement. The t‐CMSA film exhibits a bleached‐state t 50 of 80 min. The corresponding quasi‐solid‐state device shows 6.5% optical decay after 1.5 h at open circuit, bleaching/coloration times of 1.86/2.93 s, a coloration efficiency of 1026 cm 2 C −1 , and approximately 90% retention of optical modulation after 30,000 cycles. These results identify ligand geometry and steric side groups as vital parameters for regulating charge relaxation and ion retention.

title: On the formation of lipid nanoparticles and encapsulation of RNA: kinetics, dynamics, and self-assembly regimes
abstract: RNA-containing lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) form through self-assembly triggered by micromixing of an organic lipid solution against an aqueous antisolvent, leading to supersaturation and consequent nanoprecipitation. The kinetics of this process remain poorly understood. Here, we employ millisecond-resolved flowthrough small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) coupled to a multi-inlet vortex mixer (MIVM), confined impinging jets mixer (CIJM) and a T-junction mixer, to experimentally investigate the earliest stages of LNP self-assembly. Ordered LNPs show a characteristic high-q feature indicative of the ionizable lipid-RNA complex; changes in the evolution, shape, and intensity of this peak and the overall particle size in the low-q feature reveal changes in particle assembly and RNA cargo encapsulation. Results captured within milliseconds of mixing show that under turbulent flow (water/ethanol ratio 3:1), LNPs are fully formed by as early as 12 ms, including liquid-crystalline internal organization that indicates RNA encapsulation. Adjusting the water/ethanol ratio to 1:1 results in LNPs with a less ordered nanostructure, in line with reports that downstream processing plays a major role in the final structure of particles formed under these solvent conditions. These findings shed light on the mechanisms by which mixing conditions influence LNP formation. We propose a framework of four distinct self-assembly pathways defined by mixing time (i.e. faster or slower than the O(10ms) self-assembly time) and loading strategy (i.e. RNA introduced during the LNP self-assembly step, or in a second step). This provides a basis for understanding how mixing and loading strategies govern LNP formation and homogeneous RNA encapsulation, particularly for high molecular weight RNA payloads. The results establish process-structure-function relationships that support rational optimization for LNP manufacturing processes.

title: Evidence for p-wave magnetism in electronic band structure of metallic EuSi
abstract: Abstract One active frontier of quantum-matter research is the realization of p -wave symmetry-breaking phases in fermionic systems, long exemplified by the A phase of superfluid helium-3 (refs. 1–3 ). Achieving p -wave superconductivity 4 and its magnetic analogue 5 —characterized by a time-reversal-symmetric, p -wave spin-polarized Fermi surface—remains a grand challenge 6,7 . Despite recent progress in identifying candidate p -wave magnets 5,7–10 , spin-resolved spectroscopic evidence for their electronic structures remains limited. Here we report angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and spin-ARPES evidence for p -wave magnetism in the near-Fermi-level electronic structure of stoichiometric metallic EuSi, supported by symmetry analysis, first-principles calculations and neutron scattering. Neutron diffraction reveals a chiral spiral phase between 33.4 K and 62 K that fulfils archetypal p -wave magnetism criteria: it preserves the combined symmetry of time reversal and lattice translation, while breaking inversion symmetry. Spin-integrated ARPES reveals a pronounced magnetism-driven reconstruction of the electronic structure, with energy separations exceeding 100 meV, and spin-ARPES resolves S y polarization in near-Fermi-level spectral features. The extracted S y exhibits a sign-changing modulation across successive magnetic Brillouin zones and is suppressed near the nodal regions, consistent with the predicted p -wave spin texture and unfolded spin-polarization calculations. Magnetic force microscopy and micro-ARPES further reveal approximately 10-μm chiral magnetic domains. These results identify EuSi as a stoichiometric metallic platform for investigating p -wave magnetism in electronic band structures and spin-symmetry-based functionalities in spintronics 10 , topological matter 7 , superconductivity 11 and beyond.

title: Closest relatives of poxviruses prevail in human and animal guts worldwide
abstract: Abstract Large and giant double-stranded DNA viruses substantially affect eukaryotic ecology and evolution 1–4 . They prevail in the environment but are rarely found in the digestive system of animals 5,6 . Here we present the discovery of a diversified group of DNA viruses with large linear genomes, dubbed egoviruses, that comprise a putative viral order most closely related to animal-infecting poxviruses. Egoviruses are found worldwide, almost exclusively in the digestive system of humans, livestock and wild animals. The most prevalent human-specific egovirus is spread across continents, demonstrating a long-term association between egoviruses and the human gut microbiome. Eukaryotic homologues of egovirus core genes suggest that these viruses primarily infect Trichostomatia (ciliates), which assist ruminant digestive processes 7 , and Parabasalia (Metamonada), which influence animal immunity and gut microbiome ecology 8 . Egoviruses also contributed to the genetic makeup of polintons, endogenous viruses that proliferated in genomes of Trichomonas vaginalis 9 and its close Parabasalia relatives. Unlike poxviruses that form brick-shaped virions, egoviruses are predicted to form multilayered icosahedral capsids resembling those of asfuviruses and probably representing the ancestral virion structure. Egoviruses are the only known clade of double-stranded DNA viruses of eukaryotes prevailing in the animal digestive system. Phylogenomic analysis suggests an evolutionary scenario whereby egovirus-like ancestors of poxviruses infected anaerobic unicellular eukaryotes inside the gut of ancestral animals, before transitioning to animal cell infection, which was accompanied by the virion metamorphosis.

title: Tropical land-use intensification restructures biodiversity
abstract: Abstract Tropical land-use intensification threatens global biodiversity, yet most assessments of tropical agricultural landscapes focus on local-scale biodiversity, overlooking how land use restructures biodiversity across space and multiple taxa. Here we provide an ecosystem-wide assessment of 24 taxonomic groups across all domains of life—encompassing 40,049 species—along a land-use intensification gradient from lowland forests to intensively managed smallholder cash-crop monocultures in Indonesian landscapes. Despite widespread losses of landscape and local multidiversity 1 in monocultures (approximately 78% and 50%, respectively), we found no evidence for consistent community homogenization with land-use intensification. Instead, monocultures exhibit a systematic shift from turnover to nestedness for aboveground taxa. Such patterns of differentiation may mask trajectories towards biotic homogenization via early stages of assemblage simplification. Biotic differentiation has the potential to partly mitigate biodiversity losses by positively affecting γ-diversity. This opens management options, including the conservation of existing remnants of traditional agriculture and the implementation of sustainable management practices 2–4 . Our results demonstrate that tropical land-use intensification restructures biodiversity not only through species loss, but also via a pervasive reorganization of community composition across trophic levels. Conserving tropical biodiversity, therefore, requires a multi-taxon, landscape-scale perspective that explicitly integrates agricultural land uses with the protection of natural and semi-natural habitats to reconcile agricultural production and conservation.

title: Analogue simulation of massive relativistic quantum fields in 2 + 1 dimensions
abstract: Abstract Quantum field theories provide fundamental models of complex interacting systems 1–3 , from high-energy physics and cosmology to condensed matter. However, solving these models in non-perturbative and dynamical regimes is often challenging, particularly in more than one spatial dimension. Analogue simulation using tunable synthetic quantum systems can both verify existing theoretical predictions and lead to physical insights. Here we realize analogue simulation of massive relativistic quantum fields in 2 + 1 dimensions (two spatial dimensions and time), using two coherently coupled spin components 4,5 in a uniform two-dimensional atomic Bose–Einstein condensate 6,7 . Specifically, we encode the paradigmatic sine-Gordon model 8,9 in the long-wavelength modes of the field describing the relative phase, ϕ , of the two components. In the perturbative regime, collective field excitations exhibit a relativistic dispersion with a tunable mass gap. We also observe explicitly non-perturbative phenomena, including the existence of topological domain walls across which ϕ rapidly winds by 2π (ref. 10 ). Our work opens possibilities for studies of cosmologically relevant phenomena including preheating 11,12 , dynamics of topological defects 13,14 and relativistic false-vacuum decay 15–19 .
